events.title: Devlog #9: Raiders, Bleach and Next Fest
events.summary: The Clearance Defence demo is out on Steam, and it's free. Clearance Defence is in Steam Next Fest from 19 to 26 October, and the full game launches on 30 October. The demo is the first three nights of the campaign, with Endless Mode on each night you clear. You don't need to wait for the fest to play it. The new night, the raiders, the Bleach Tower and the defender orders below all come later in the campaign, so they aren't in the demo. They're in the full game on the 30th. Night 8: The Hollow

events.title: Devlog #7: Fighting Fire with Fire
events.summary: Fighting Fire with Fire It has been a busy few weeks since Devlog #6, so this one is a proper catch-up. Night 4 has stopped being the end of the road, the whole game has learned to play on a controller, and the difficulty finally climbs the way I always wanted it to. All of it is live in the Steam Playtest right now at v0.85.0. One thing up front, and I mean it: the headline stuff here is brand new and I have not had nearly enough eyes on it. events.title: Closing time, and the doors are open to everyone
events.summary: The Clearance Defence Playtest is open to everyone this weekend. No waitlist, no waiting to be let in. If you fancy holding a supermarket against a tide of garden gnomes after dark, you can walk straight in. Here's the situation. It's closing time, the lights are down, and the Summer stock wants the clearance aisle. events.title: Devlog #6 — Morale, Fire and a Fourth Night
events.summary: A fourth night The campaign has grown by a night. Night 4 plays start to finish now — dialogue and voice acting in, its beats playing through properly. We kept its roster deliberately tight: one fresh foe, so we can tune how it plays against everything you've built up by the time you reach it, rather than balancing five things badly at once. events.title: Three Nights Down — v0.60 closes the loop on Playtest
events.summary: A run from start to finish v0.60.0 closes the loop. You can play the demo through to the end now — three nights, all the way through — and the game has somewhere to land you when you win. When the final wave of Night 3 breaks, a Thanks for Playing scene plays. It's quiet, it matches the main-menu styling, and it has a Discord link on it because the most useful thing a finished player can do is tell us what they thought. events.title: Devlog #4: A Handle on the Lever — v0.45.0
events.summary: Towers can run dry now. Every other change in v0.45.0 is a tool we've handed you for dealing with it. The headline change: towers run out of ammunition. Every shot decrements the magazine, and a tower stops firing when it's empty. The first time your projectile tower goes quiet halfway through a wave is the moment everything else in this update starts to make sense. events.title: Devlog #3: After Closing Time
events.summary: Every night, after the last customer leaves and the lights go down, a war begins. The Easter goods — reduced to clear, still on the shelf — defend their aisles against the Summer stock pushing in from the back. Garden gnomes in makeshift cardboard armour. Waves of them, every night, before morning saves everyone. The store staff don't know. That's the point. events.title: Devlog #2: Morale, Rebalancing, and the Playtest Is Open
events.summary: A lot has changed since the last devlog. Here's what happened. Morale Easter Defence Force units now have feelings. Specifically, they have morale — and it affects how hard they hit. Morale rises when waves go well and drops when things fall apart. Lose a tower and the troops notice. Finish a wave without casualties and they're emboldened. events.title: Devlog #1: Night 2 Takes Shape and Steam Builds Go Live
events.summary: This is the first weekly devlog for Clearance Defence. The plan is simple: every week, write up what actually happened in development. No polish, no spin. Just what got built, what broke, and what we learned. This week was a big one. Versions v0.18.0 through v0.23.0, and a lot of pieces falling into place.
